issues.title: The page doesn't explain what happened after reject
issues.summary: After the wallet rejection, the modal shows only a generic "Transaction Failed / Something went wrong." with a Retry link. It never says the user rejected the request, so a deliberate cancel looks like a protocol or network failure. Detect the wallet's user-rejected error (code 4001 / ACTION_REJECTED) and show something like "Request rejected in wallet" with Retry, not the generic failure text.
stepsToReproduce: Reject the flow's main request in the wallet (error 4001).
issues.expected: Show that the request was rejected and let the user try again.

issues.title: The page doesn't explain what happened after wrong network
issues.summary: On the wrong network, the app sent the stake anyway and then showed a 'Transaction Failed' modal saying 'User denied the transaction signature.' The page still says 'Network: Ethereum', and the only option is 'Retry', which will fail the same way. Compare the wallet's chainId with the expected chain before sending, show a 'Switch to Ethereum' prompt (wallet_switchEthereumChain), and map chain-mismatch errors to a wrong-network message instead of 'user denied'.
stepsToReproduce: Start with the wallet on Sepolia instead of Ethereum.
issues.expected: Notice the wrong network and ask the wallet to switch before sending anything.

issues.title: The page doesn't explain what happened after switch account
issues.summary: After the account switch the app shows "Transaction Failed – User denied the transaction signature." with a Retry link, which is wrong: the user didn't deny anything, and the rejection likely means the transaction was still set to come from the old account. Listen for the wallet's accountsChanged event, rebuild the pending transaction for the new address, and show a message like "Account changed, please review and confirm again"; the header (0xe00C...6aD2b5) doesn't show which account is in use now.
stepsToReproduce: Switch the wallet to account B right before the step that triggers the first signing request.
issues.expected: Use the newly selected account for everything that follows.

checks.label: Matches the button
checks.detail: The Stake button and the 'You are staking 0.05 ETH' popup match an eth_sendTransaction to Lido's stETH contract (0xae7ab965…fE84) calling submit(address) with 0.05 ETH. Token, amount and recipient contract all match. The submit() argument is only a referral tag (here the user's own address) and doesn't redirect funds; stETH is minted to the sender. There are no approvals or permits, and only 0.05 ETH leaves the wallet. The simulation doesn't show the incoming stETH, likely a simulator gap.
